current_answer: Interledger Foundation has paused applications for its 2026 Local Impact Mini-Grants. Its earlier announcement advertised rolling submissions through 11 November, but the current programme page and application form both say applications are paused. Individuals, community groups, and local fintech startups should not spend time preparing a submission for this cycle unless the issuer reopens it; the USD 500–3,000 project grant remains described, but the application route is unavailable now.

catalogue_card.question: Interledger’s 11 November date no longer means you can apply.
catalogue_card.text: The foundation’s current programme page and form say its USD 500–3,000 Local Impact Mini-Grant applications are paused. Its July announcement still says rolling applications through 11 November. Wait for an issuer reopening notice before preparing the two-page concept note.

summary: Interledger’s current programme page and application form say applications are paused. The form cites more than 600 applications from more than 60 countries.
The earlier 11 November 2026 end date is historical guidance, not current access to the form.
The USD 500–3,000 grant is for direct local financial-access project activities, not operating costs or an award guarantee.
No reopening date is published; check the current issuer page before starting an application.
uncertainty: Interledger has not published a reopening date or new cutoff; the form did not establish whether drafts can still be completed.
The grant range is not an award guarantee, and sanctions and project-purpose restrictions still apply if applications reopen.
NLnet’s revised GenAI policy remains unpublished; Microsoft and Cloudflare contradictions remain unresolved.
The catalogue does not verify every programme or every country.
freshness_note: Interledger’s programme page, application form, and earlier announcement were checked on 2026-09-29. The current pause controls over the older 11 November window.
